textbookText: At first mass of a clean and dry calorimeter with its stirrer is measured. About two- third volume
of the calorimeter is filled with water. Again, the mass of the calorimeter with stirrer and water
is measured. Then, the calorimeter is placed inside insulating system of wooden box, and a
thermometer is inserted into it as shown in figure 11.7. The initial temperature of the
calorimeter with stirrer and water is noted.
After this, certain mass of dry pieces of melting ice are introduced in to the calorimeter. To
make ice pieces dry blotting paper are used. Then the mixture is stirred well until ice melts
completely. The steady temperature of mixture is noted. After complete melting of ice, reading
of the thermometer remains steady for a moment. Now, the calorimeter is taken out from the
wooden box, and the mass of mixture is measured.
Let, Mass of a calorimeter with stirrer = m1

Workout Example: Q. Evaporation of perspiration is an important mechanism for temperature control of warm-blooded animals. What mass of water must be evaporated from the surface of an 80 kg human body to cool it by 1C? The specific heat capacity of the human body is approximately 420 J kg–1K–1, and the latent heat of vaporization of water at the body temperature is 2.4106J kg–1.

Solution: Here, Heat liberated from the surface of an 80 kg human body (having Sp. heat capacity 0.1 cal g– l C–1) to cool by 1C is given by, Q 1 = m s = 80 × 420 × 1 = 33600J Let mw be the mass of water that is evaporated from the human body. Heat required to evaporate is given by, Q2 = mw L = mw × 2.4106 = 2.4106 mw Here, L = 577calg-1C is the latent heat of vaporization of water at the body temperature.
According to question, Q 1 = Q 2 or, 33600 = 2.4106 mw or, mw = 2.4106 33600 = 1.3910-2 kg. Hence, 1.3910-2 kg mass of water must evaporate from the surface of given human body.

Q. How much heat is required to convert 10 g ice at –10C into steam at 100C? (Sp. heat capacity of ice is 2100 J kg-1K-1, Sp. heat capacity of water is 4200 J kg-1 K-1, latent heat of vaporization of water is 2.26106 J kg-1 and latent heat of fusion of ice is 3.36105 J kg-1).

Solution: Here, Mass of ice (mi) = 10 g = 10-2 kg Sp. heat of ice (Si) = 2100 J kg-1K-1 Latent heat of fusion of ice (Li) = 3.36105 J kg-1 Latent heat of vaporization of water (Lv) = 2.26106 J kg-1 Specific heat capacity of water (Sw) = 4200 J kg-1 K-1 Heat required (Q) =?

Now, heat required to change temperature of 10 g ice from –10C to 0oC is given by Q1 = mi si = 10-2 × 2100 × [0 – (–10)] = 210J Amount of heat required to convert ice at 0C into water at 0C is given by Q2 = mi Li = 10-2 × 3.36105 = 3.36103J Amount of heat required to convert water at 0C to water at 100C is given by Q3 = mi sw = 10-2 × 4200 × 100 = 4200J Amount of heat required to convert water at 100C to steam at 100C is given by Q4 = mi Lv = 10-2 × 2.26106 = 2.26104J Therefore, the total amount of heat required is given by Q = Q1 + Q2 + Q3 +Q4= (210 + 3.36103 + 4200 + 2.26104)J = 3.02104J Hence, 3.02104J heat is required.
